# Deliverable 5 — GitHub Skills and Open-Source Inventory

**Research date:** 26 November 2026 · **Repositories inspected:** 85 · **Not inspected (listed, with reasons):** 27 · **Full notes, security observations and commit hashes:** [Appendix E](appendix/E-open-source-inventory.md)

Every entry below was inspected by reading its actual files — README, licence file, source code or skill text, and dependency list — at a recorded commit. **Nothing was installed or executed.** Descriptions are of what the code really does, not what the repository claims.

| Verdict | Count | Meaning |
|---|:-:|---|
| Reuse directly | 26 | Permissive licence, maintained, does what it says |
| Reuse with changes | 18 | Useful, but must be adapted, restricted or verified first |
| Reference only | 23 | Read for ideas; do not depend on it |
| Avoid | 18 | Licence, security, maintenance or marketplace-terms problem |

## Bottom line

**There is no open-source "digital shelf" product to install.** What exists is (1) solid general-purpose building blocks with permissive licences, (2) "skills" — text instructions for an AI assistant — of very uneven quality, and (3) things that look free but are not: licences that forbid commercial use, cap it by company revenue or can oblige us to publish our own code, and scraping tools built to evade marketplaces' defences.

Two findings matter most:

- **No marketplace publishes an open-source tool that hands over competitor or shelf data.** Amazon's official open-source material (connector, samples, developer MCP servers) gives access to *our own* seller or vendor data. No official Walmart MCP server was found. Competitor listings, search rankings and third-party reviews are not available through any open-source tool that also respects marketplace terms.
- **"Free" often has strings attached.** Examples found: an image-quality library licensed for non-commercial use only; Pimcore, now free only below €5 million revenue; n8n's "fair-code" licence; AGPL and SSPL tools; an Arabic language model with a custom share-alike licence; and several repositories with no licence file at all — which means no right to reuse.

## What Build 1 already uses from this inventory

| Building block | Used for | Licence |
|---|---|---|
| pgvector | Meaning-based search inside PostgreSQL | PostgreSQL licence |
| Transformers.js with the multilingual-e5-small model | Creating embeddings on our own server — no brand content leaves it | Apache-2.0 (library), MIT (model) |
| unpdf | Reading PDFs | MIT |
| sharp | Reading image dimensions | Apache-2.0 |
| Zod | Validating every form and every research data file | MIT |
| Playwright | Browser tests | Apache-2.0 |

Document parsing for Word, PowerPoint and Excel, the job queue and barcode validation were written in-house in a few hundred lines each rather than adding dependencies; pg-boss is the recommended upgrade if job volumes grow.

## Adopt next (Stages 3–5)

| What | For | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| Amazon's official SP-API SDK and samples | Reading our own listings, issues, A+ Content and reports | Needs an approved Selling Partner API application |
| extruct and price-parser | Reading product facts that pages publish for search engines | Only on pages we are permitted to collect |
| Crawlee and Playwright | Page collection where a site's terms allow it | Robots.txt respected; "avoid detection" features switched off |
| json-rules-engine | Storing content rules as data | — |
| pg-boss | Scheduled and background jobs | When the built-in queue is outgrown |
| OpenCV (with sharp) | Background whiteness, sharpness, frame-fill checks on images | — |
| Docling or MarkItDown | Difficult PDFs with tables; retailer style guides | — |
| Prompt material from Anthropic's skills and two Amazon listing skill packs | Starting drafts for our own AI instructions | Every marketplace rule in them must be verified against the requirements library first |

## Five rules for the team

1. **No licence file, no reuse.** A one-line "MIT" in a README is not enough.
2. **Check the model's licence as well as the code's.** At least two tools have permissive code but default to models not cleared for commercial use.
3. **Marketplace data comes through the marketplace's own API or a licensed provider.** Page collection is for our own sites and for retailers whose terms allow it.
4. **A "skill" is a draft written by a stranger.** Read it, verify every rule, remove the advertising, then make it ours. One skill pack inspected scrapes Amazon and contains a code-injection bug.
5. **Pin and lock every dependency, turn telemetry off, and give AI tools read-only keys.** Two repositories in this review document real supply-chain compromises of popular packages during 2026.

## Limitations

- Repositories were read statically from shallow copies; very large ones were read selectively.
- GitHub issue trackers, security advisories and "archived" flags could not be reached, so maintenance status rests on commit dates and release notes.
- Model licences come from the publishers' model cards.
- The web-search allowance ran out during discovery, so some candidates were not found or checked.
- This is engineering due diligence, not legal advice. Have counsel confirm licence conclusions before anything is distributed outside the company.
